items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Satch and I used to, uh, pal around together.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. Lots of musicians in. Lots of musicians. Who were some of the other ones that you... What were the other ones that you...

Well, uh... Milford Piron, my teacher. Armand Piron. Thank you. Louis Cottrell's daddy. Bonnie Bigard, the Teos. Lorenzo Junior, Lorenzo Senior. Big I, Louis. Well, we could just go on and name quite a number of them. Piku.
The guys your age, how many of them are there? Let's see.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: as far back as I can remember, when I was a little kid... I'd break my neck to go over there and listen to them

ctx.x: Well, let's see. We're going to talk about a whole lot of different things, like I'd gotten a letter from Laurie Wright, and he wanted a little more information on Lewis Armstrong. Where did you first hear Louis Armstrong?

Well, as far back as I can remember, when I was a little kid, when this particular group of boys would parade on the streets, I'd break my neck to go over there and listen to them. And sometimes they came right down to San Antonio Street, which was about, well, in between the two blocks that I lived. I lived on Robinson and the parade would come down San Antonio Street. I don't know, I don't know, they had a hymn there. How did that happen? What were they doing? Well, just parading, I imagine. I can't recall…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: I just want to say that, that Louis Armstrong is the only one that happened to mention in his biography of George Moret.

ctx.x: I know Natty said he was raised that way.

On French, that's right. And I still talk French now. And then when someone, when I can talk with someone. So the first lesson I had at Nelson Jean's house, he was a great friend of the family, but he liked to take a drink of wine. So I went on my first lesson. And then, while he told me to get, had an old cornet that I bought somewhere. I don't know where it was. And anyhow, my daddy found it for me, I believe. And I was too young to remember. He wanted me to learn how to clean the horn. So I decided to clean…
We talked to one of the brothers of the old men. There was an old Lorenzo and a Louis Teo, Papa Teo.
